system.name: Mu Cephei
system.description: Known as Herschel's Garnet Star for its intense ruby-red colour, Mu Cephei is one of the largest and most luminous red supergiants in the Milky Way, about 2,800 light-years away in Cepheus. It lies within the Cepheus OB2 stellar association and is in the late stages of stellar evolution.

mucephei.name: Mu Cephei
mucephei.description: An M2 Ia red supergiant about 1,035 times the diameter of the Sun, so luminous that it radiates roughly 340,000 times the Sun's total power. Its dramatic red-garnet colour is caused by titanium oxide absorption in its cool, extended atmosphere. It is a semi-regular variable and is approaching the end of its life.
mucephei.funFact: Sir William Herschel described Mu Cephei as 'a very fine deep garnet-coloured star' in 1783 — giving it the nickname Herschel's Garnet Star that astronomers still use today.
